items.title: A better model will not make a better scribe overnight
items.body: By the host's own account the new model is no better than its cheaper sibling for most everyday work, and costs more per task. Summarising a consultation is everyday work. If a scribe supplier announces an upgrade to the newest model, ask what measurably improved in their own testing, and whether the price changes.

items.title: The failure to watch for has changed
items.body: Ethan Mollick's observation is that the errors are no longer invented facts but poor judgement: work that is too long, and no sense of when it is not good enough. In a clinical note that means plausible, accurate and bloated, with the important line buried. Reading the note critically matters more, not less, and brevity is worth specifying.

items.title: Science claims are the vendor's, and early
items.body: The gene therapy and protein design results come from Anthropic's own launch material and have not been independently replicated or peer reviewed. They are interesting for research, and irrelevant to prescribing for now. Ed Zitron has published nothing on this release, so there is no opposing source; the scepticism here is mine.
